facts.statement: K3 SoC integrates 8 X100 general-purpose cores and 8 A100 AI cores (2 A100 clusters, 60 TOPS aggregate AI compute) using RISC-V homogeneous fusion: scalar (standard ISA), vector (RVV 1.0) and matrix (IME extension) compute share one RISC-V programming model, and standard Linux threads drive AI computation without a heterogeneous scheduler or driver management.

facts.statement: A100 execution resources (Preview 2026-01-29 description, to be reconciled with production hardware at board porting): each of the 2 A100 clusters comprises 4 scalar cores, 2 vector cores, 2 local-memory banks and a shared L2; the Tensor Core (IME-2.0, 1024/2048-bit datapath) is shared by two compute cores and accepts one MMA instruction per cycle from each; a per-core private IME-1.0 unit (256/512-bit, INT8xINT8->INT32 small MAC) also exists; each core has an independent 512-bit load channel and the front end dual-issues one 512-bit load plus one MMA per cycle.

facts.statement: A100 IME tile shapes and implementation parameters (LMUL=1 tiles): INT4 x INT4 -> INT32 tile 8x32x8; INT8 x INT8 -> INT32 tile 8x16x8 (integer family: lambda=4, MUL_C=2, SEW=32); FP16/BF16 x FP16/BF16 -> FP32 tile 8x8x8 (MUL_C=2, SEW=32); 4:2 structured sparse: INT4 8x64x8, INT8 8x32x8; block-scaled integer (Int4/Int8 + FP16/BF16 scale -> FP16/BF16): lambda=8, MUL_C=1, SEW=16, tiles 8x32x8 (Int4) / 8x16x8 (Int8); sliding-window variants keep their base family tile. lambda is fixed per instruction family and NOT configurable via vtype; MUL_C = VLEN/(SEW x lambda^2).
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/bd69e01a6280ae5ab4493ea82b0e819fb34f093da43c264fc3be3c6291a8c6c8/ime_extension.md.search.txt:274-317 (2.1.2),371-396 (2.5),2313-2329 (App. A)

facts.statement: IME operand and data-layout contract: vs1 holds tile A (row-major), vs2 holds tile B (column-major); B^T in the semantics C <- C + A x B^T is a geometric layout statement and does NOT require a software transpose of B; vd holds both the initial accumulator and the result with an implementation-defined result layout; Int4 inputs use packed nibble storage (element 2n in bits [3:0], 2n+1 in bits [7:4] of byte n); EEW=8/16 use standard linear vector element ordering; integer signedness variants (none/u/us/su) select signed/unsigned interpretation of A and B with the accumulator always signed.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/bd69e01a6280ae5ab4493ea82b0e819fb34f093da43c264fc3be3c6291a8c6c8/ime_extension.md.search.txt:67-86 (1.4),144-155 (1.5),437-479 (2.7),529-538 (4.2)

facts.statement: IME register budget and granularity: input matrices A and B each occupy a single vector register (LMUL=1 only; every other LMUL encoding reserved and illegal in IME instructions); the accumulator tile occupies MUL_C registers - MUL_C=2 for the integer and fp16/bf16-fp32 families (vd even-numbered, vd+vd+1 group) and MUL_C=1 for the block-scaled families (any vd); the destination group must not overlap vs1/vs2; MUL_C is fixed per Profile, not a dynamically configurable parameter; sparse paths additionally consume v0/v1 (recovery masks) and scale paths v0/v1 (scale parameters), so those paths have 30 generally usable vector registers.

assumptions.statement: Standard RISC-V unprivileged semantics hold for the non-universal integer cases (wrap-around signed overflow, division/remainder by zero defined not trapping, shift amounts masked to the operand width) and standard RVV 1.0 FP semantics (frm-controlled rounding) via RVA23 compliance; the pack states RVA23* compliance but does not restate these behaviours.
assumptions.why_needed: The compiler's arithmetic lowering and basic-optimization legality conditions depend on integer overflow/div/shift semantics; the target documents only profile compliance.
assumptions.validation_method: Bounded probe under the declared QEMU endpoint (div-by-zero, overwide shift, wrap cases, an frm rounding check) and re-verification on the board at porting; until then treat as RISC-V-standard.

assumptions.statement: Vector and scalar memory operands are naturally aligned; the compiler emits aligned accesses with masked tails and does not rely on misaligned access support. The pack does not state misaligned or out-of-range access behaviour for A100.
assumptions.why_needed: Predicated/tail lowering and wide-access grouping legality depend on the alignment contract.
assumptions.validation_method: Bounded misaligned-access probe under the declared QEMU endpoint (expect exception or defined behaviour, recorded either way); on-board check at porting; keep aligned-plus-mask codegen until verified.

assumptions.statement: The FMA contraction/rounding detail of smt.vfwmadot (single-rounding fused versus two-rounding widen-then-multiply-add) is not specified by the IME v0.6 document; no exactness claim may rely on it. Floating outputs are compared within each case's declared tolerance, so either behaviour is within policy.
assumptions.why_needed: The spec gives program-visible semantics as fp32 accumulate but not the rounding-point contract.
assumptions.validation_method: If a case ever demands it, differential comparison of the executed instruction result against an independent fp32 reference at the used shapes; otherwise treat as tolerance-covered.

assumptions.statement: The formal memory model between A100 harts is assumed RVWMO (implied by RVA23 profile compliance) with per-level cache coherence as documented (MESI L1 D, MOESI L2 per cluster); the pack does not state the cross-cluster ordering contract. Generated cross-worker communication therefore uses explicit pthread/atomic synchronization and does not assume timing-based visibility.
assumptions.why_needed: Cross-worker merge correctness and any future reordering optimization depend on the visibility rule; only per-cache coherence protocols are documented.
assumptions.validation_method: On-board memory-ordering probes during porting (write-visibility across clusters with and without fences); under the pinned QEMU the guest is a single coherent address space so the assumption is untested there.

assumptions.statement: TCM, DMA and hardware-spinlock software interfaces (allocation, completion, visibility, lifetime) are unverified, and under the pinned QEMU endpoint these MMIO regions are not part of the userspace execution path; no generated code may assume TCM/DMA availability or asynchronous reuse until the interfaces are verified.
assumptions.why_needed: The manuals document the hardware but not the software allocation/completion contracts; the Preview's async-DMA dataflow needs matching SDK sources and probes.
assumptions.validation_method: Match SDK sources and run on-board probes (spacemit-tcm-smi resource state, TCM allocation/DMA completion/visibility) before any use; the correctness path uses Linux userspace memory only.

assumptions.statement: The production pairing of the shared IME-2.0 matrix engines (Preview: shared by two compute cores) and the actual allowed A100 core set (official examples use core IDs 8-15) are unverified on hardware; QEMU guest threads establish neither. Resource evidence under QEMU records guest threads, work partition and dynamic instruction counts, never physical core identities.
assumptions.why_needed: Work placement and matrix-throughput reasoning depend on the real topology; the Preview is an architectural description that production hardware must confirm.
assumptions.validation_method: On-board discovery during the porting step (probe eligible cores, confirm engine pairing and usable storage); extend assumption A001.
